To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the one-to-one genotype-to-phenotype mapping assumption is not empirically sustainable in molecular biology and that the subliminal and convenient one-to-one genotype to phenotype mapping assumption in biology and medicine may be upheld because it is convenient to the private appropriation and commercialization of scientific discoveries.

(i) the subliminal and often explicit one-to-one genotype-to-phenotype mapping assumption (GPM) is untenable in the post-genomic era; and (ii) that this assumption may be upheld because it is convenient and convenient to private appropriation and marketing.
the subliminal and convenient assumption of one-to-one mapping of genotype-phenotype in molecular biology and evolutionary biology is not empirically sustainable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what constitutes the fundamental units of biology, the nature of the causal relationships between these units and the nature of biological causation itself.
a systems and nonlinear approach to biology and the question of how such a perspective can contribute to the development of more sustainable and integrative science.
the epistemological and ontological implications of the transition from the reductionist paradigm to a more integrative one, in the context of post-genomic biology.

a linear causation scheme cannot explain the observed phenomena and the subliminal one-to-one genotype-to-phenotype mapping assumption is untenable in the post-genomic era.
the linear causal schemes in post-genomic molecular biology and evolutionary biology are not empirically sustainable.
the one-to-one mapping assumption is not sustainable in post-genomics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we argue that the linear causation schemes that underpin the flow of information paradigm in molecular biology and the signaling pathway paradigm in systems biology are not valid anymore.
we question the validity in post-genomic science of the one-to-one genotype phenotype mapping (GPM), which is a basic assumption in molecular biology and evolutionary theory.
the one-to-one genotype-to-phenotype mapping assumption is not sustainable in post-genomics and systems biology.

a systems perspective and nonlinear dynamical modeling is necessary for the understanding of the complexity of biological processes.
